response.title: is a solar generator worth the money
response.answer:
A solar generator can be worth the money, but usually for backup power and convenience—not for saving money on electricity.

The biggest factor is how you plan to use it.

A solar generator is essentially a rechargeable battery with an inverter, often paired with portable solar panels. Unlike a gas generator, it doesn't produce electricity from fuel. It stores electricity from the wall or solar panels.

When is a solar generator worth it?

Use case

	

Worth it?

	

Why




Emergency power outages

	

 Yes

	

Quiet, indoor-safe backup for essentials




Camping and RV trips

	

 Yes

	

Portable, no gasoline needed




Reducing home electricity bills

	

 Usually no

	

Savings are often too small




Running a refrigerator during outages

	

 Yes

	

A sufficiently large unit can keep food cold




Powering an entire house

	

 Depends

	

Requires a large, expensive system




Replacing a gas generator

	

 Depends

	

Cleaner and quieter, but limited battery capacity

How much should you spend?

Here are examples of current options at different capacities.

EcoFlow - Delta 3 Classic Portable Power Station with 160W S…

1,024 Wh battery + 160 W solar panel

$669.00

Good for basic emergency backup, electronics and some refrigerator use.

Anker - SOLIX S2000 Portable Power Station,2010Wh/Peak 3000W…

2,010 Wh battery, solar panels separate

$749.99

Better for longer outages and running several essential devices.

Will it pay for itself?

Suppose you spend $1,000 on a solar generator and panels.

If you harvest and use 1 kWh of solar electricity daily, at an assumed electricity rate of $0.15/kWh:

Daily savings: $0.15

Annual savings: $54.75

Simple payback: approximately 18.3 years

That's before battery degradation, charging losses and maintenance. Most portable systems won't be used at full capacity every day.

So if your main objective is reducing your electricity bill, a conventional home solar installation is generally a better investment. 
EnergySage
+1

How long will it actually run?

For a 2,000 Wh battery, assuming 85% usable energy:

Device

	

Approximate runtime




Wi-Fi router (15 W)

	

113 hours




Laptop (60 W)

	

28 hours




Fan (50 W)

	

34 hours




Refrigerator (average 60 W)

	

28 hours




Space heater (1,500 W)

	

1.1 hours

These are illustrative runtimes, not guarantees. Refrigerators cycle on and off, and actual consumption varies.

My recommendation: If you want emergency backup, consider buying a 1–2 kWh LiFePO4 power station first. Add solar panels if you expect multi-day outages or off-grid use. You may not need panels at all for short outages. 
Lab Tested & Ranked
+1

One question that would significantly change my recommendation:

Backup electricity during power outages
Save money on my electricity bill
Camping or RV use
Power an off-grid cabin or property
Get a recommendation for my use case
